one_liner: Twilio has a broad REST API usable via a free no-credit-card trial account, with OAuth 2.0 (client credentials and authorization code), API keys and Account SID/Auth Token over HTTP Basic; no vendor MCP is confirmed by the pages.
auth_notes: Pages confirm OAuth 2.0 (Client Credentials and Authorization Code), API keys (Main/Standard/Restricted) and Auth Token. REST requests accept HTTP Basic with Account SID + Auth Token or API key SID + secret, or an OAuth Bearer token. Organization-level APIs support OAuth 2.0 only. OAuth apps are created in the console by the account owner (self-serve).
access_notes: Homepage advertises a free trial with no credit card required and a free account to get started. Trial limits and expiry are not shown on the provided pages, so the trial classification is kept at medium confidence.
blocker_notes: Credentials come through a free trial; trial restrictions and likely upgrade to paid for production use are not verified on the pages. No MCP server is confirmed: the MCP Registry shows nothing under the vendor namespace and the pages only show a 'Building with AI' link.

evidence.quote: Sign up for a free Twilio account and grab one of our official server-side SDKs to get started.
Twilio supports two OAuth 2.0 grant types: **Client Credentials** and **Authorization Code**.
You can authenticate requests using either HTTP Basic authentication or OAuth.
For HTTP Basic authentication, use your Account SID and Auth Token or an [API key](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/api-keys) SID and secret.
Learn how to interact with the REST API for account management, development testing, and fraud protection.
Familiarize yourself with Twilio's server-side, front-end, and mobile SDKs, OpenAPI specifications and Postman collections.
